title: Orchestrate buildcache indexing and toolchain harmonization
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Summary: Reduce CI build time variance and eliminate recurrent cache misses by introducing a buildcache 'indexing' layer, consolidating language toolchains, and standardizing linter versions across repos. This ticket coordinates the orchestration: schema for cache keys, priming strategy for cold caches, cross-repo toolchain image, and CI job changes to use the indexed cache.

Background: Over the past year we've seen flaky CI runs caused by inconsistent cache keys (different hashing inputs across builders) and multiple repo-specific linter/toolchain images (node/python/go) that increase image churn and slow cache hit rates. Previous tickets tackled isolated pieces; this work harmonizes them into an incremental, low-risk rollout.

Goals: 1) Define a canonical cache key schema (repo, toolchain-version, dockerbase-hash, deps-locksum, build-profile) and implement a cache-index service (metadata-only) that reduces false negatives for cache lookups. 2) Build a consolidated, stamp-versioned toolchain image for node/python/go used by all monorepos. 3) Align linter versions (eslint, pylintrc, golangci-lint) and migration steps. 4) Add cache priming job to warm new runners and an observability dashboard to track hit-rate, median build time, and failed-cache reasons.

Implementation plan:
- Phase A (design, 1 week): finalize cache key schema and index API; produce migration playbook. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/ci-cache-index (draft).
- Phase B (proto, 1 week): land a proof-of-concept indexer service behind a feature flag; update builder templates in ./infra/ci/templates to consult index before full cache scan. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/9223 (WIP).
- Phase C (toolchain image, 1.5 weeks): build a consolidated toolchain image image:registry.redwood.io/ci/toolchain:v2025-03-01 and update a canary set of pipelines (sdk/, runtime/, console/). PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3311, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4390.
- Phase D (linter alignment, 1 week): pin eslint@8.31.0, golangci-lint v1.56.0, and migrate pylintrc to shared config; run autofix CI job for non-blocking branch updates.
- Phase E (rollout & observability, 1 week): enable indexer for 50% of runners with automatic fallback; deploy Grafana dashboard and SLO alerts. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/ci-buildcache/hit-rate

Trade-offs and risks:
- Introducing an indexer adds a metadata service dependency; mitigations: make indexer optional and ensure builders fallback to existing cache semantics on timeout.
- Consolidated toolchain image increases blast radius when changes are required; mitigation: strict image versioning, canary pipelines, and automatic revert in deployer.
- Linter upgrades may surface large numbers of lint failures; mitigation: run autofix in non-blocking mode and schedule separate cleanup tickets for noisy repos.

Success metrics:
- Increase global cache hit-rate from baseline (~62%) to >=88% for PR builds within 4 weeks of rollout.
- Reduce median PR build time from 9m to <=5m for typical fast-path builds.
- No increase in CI flake rate >5% relative baseline.

Operational notes:
- Observability will emit: cache_hit (bool), lookup_reason (list: key-mismatch|missed-deps|index-miss|stale), index_latency_ms, toolchain_image_pull_ms.
- Runbook for indexer outage: disable index feature flag on infra config and revert builder template to legacy lookup.

Next steps (owner: Owen Patel):
1) Finalize key schema doc and share with infra/engineers for review (due 2025-02-17).
2) Open infra prototype PR and request early reviewers from @kai, @sana.
3) Build initial toolchain image and smoke test in a sandbox runner.
